summary: Intermittent TLS session handoff due to SD-WAN source-port rewrite causes range-retry mismatch and shard validation errors
description:
Issue summary:
Customers running a private deployment behind a corporate SD-WAN report intermittent model shard validation failures during large, parallel range downloads. Failures correlate with a short window of 1xx-5xxs and 'shard checksum mismatch' errors from the client side.

Impact:
- Affects a single large enterprise customer (NimbusAI) on a private deployment in us-west-2.
- Intermittent: ~3-5% of range requests per large shard are failing, causing application-layer retries and higher latency.
- Some model loads fall back to smaller variants or cause request-level timeouts if retries exceed thresholds.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering + SD-WAN overlay to on-prem).
- Serving nodes in a dedicated pool in us-west-2.
- Artifact storage: S3 presigned range downloads (us-west-2).
- Customer's SD-WAN appliance rewrites source ports for egress sessions for per-flow aggregation.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Trigger a large-batch inference with gptx-13b-v2-sharded that streams 4 concurrent shard range requests per node.
2) Observe that 1 or more of the range requests fail with 403/401-like validation errors or partial writes.
3) Retry logic in client re-issues ranges; sometimes the server rejects the retry as a different session leading to checksum mismatch.

Observed logs / traces:
- Serving node nginx access logs show range requests hitting the S3 presigned URL with identical URL but different ephemeral source ports at the egress.
- TLS session establishment logs show server-side cert validation passes, but client-side logs show TLS session resumption failures immediately before a failed range.
- Packet captures (pcap) from customer's egress show SD-WAN rewriting source port for subsequent packets within the same logical connection.
- Control plane traces show short-lived auth token refreshes concurrent with range retry windows.

Initial hypothesis:
- The customer's SD-WAN is performing source-port rewrite/NAT aggregation for flows. When a range retry is issued on a re-used HTTP/2 connection or pooled HTTP/1.1 connection, the egress rewrite causes the cloud-side connection allocator or presigned-url validation to attribute traffic to a different TCP flow. This leads to TLS session mismatch or S3 range request validation rejecting the retry, resulting in partial downloads and checksum failures.

Why this is unique/different from typical NAT issues:
- Not classic ephemeral port exhaustion — packets arrive but are rewritten mid-session.
- Manifests only with parallel range downloads that exercise connection pooling and HTTP multiplexing.

Immediate mitigation attempted by customer:
- Disabled connection pooling and forced single concurrent range per client process -> observed drop in failure rate to ~0.2%.
- Added a small random delay between parallel range requests -> reduced collisions but not eliminated.

Requested from customer/support:
- Full pcap around a failed range (provided).
- Topology diagram of SD-WAN egress behavior (provided).
- Repro script and exact client/SDK versions (provided).

Next steps we recommend / will perform:
- Reproduce in controlled lab using SD-WAN emulator that rewrites source ports mid-flow.
- Add additional logging in serving runtime to correlate TLS session IDs, ephemeral ports and presigned-url signature verification events.
- Work with engineering to determine if we can make range retries include a short single-use token tied to the original session to tolerate egress-port rewrite.
- Engage NimbusAI networking team to disable source-port rewrite for presigned-url flows as a customer-side workaround.

investigation_notes: Reproduced locally with SD-WAN emulator that rewrites ephemeral source port after TCP handshake. When HTTP/2 stream retry is re-sent, back-end session manager rejected packets due to mismatch in 5-tuple -> retry dropped or attributed to new session.

S3 presigned URLs are valid independent of TCP session, but client-side library expects connection affinity for range checks; mid-flow rewrite breaks assumptions in both client and our edge TCP session mapping.
Control-plane auth refreshes aligned with the same time window because retries trigger client SDK to re-authorize; need to decouple that from retry logic when rewriting is detected.
Packet-level evidence: identical TCP sequence numbers but different source ports for fragments of the same high-level request after rewrite event.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Customer disabled SD-WAN source-port rewrite for traffic to Redwood artifact endpoints and re-enabled connection pooling. Failure rate fell to <0.1% during 48h verification.

Planned long-term fix: Engineering will prototype a session-fingerprint header for retries (x-rw-session) so that server-side acceptance can be tolerant to source-port changes for a short grace window. INT ticket opened for implementation and PR referenced.

Follow-ups:
- INT-900201: Instrument TLS/session IDs in artifact fetch path (priority P2).
- ENG-PR-4382: Prototype server-side retry-fingerprint acceptance (owner: Diego).
- Customer follow-up scheduled: 2026-03-20 post-mitigation review.
